messagedraft.title: Draft Email
messagedraft.subject: Following up on the project timeline
messagedraft.body:
I wanted to follow up on our conversation from last Tuesday. We're making good progress on the timeline, but I'd love to sync before Thursday's review. Would a 30-minute call on Wednesday afternoon work for you?

I'll have the updated milestones ready by then, should only take a few minutes to walk through.

dialogue.title: Interview Script
dialogue.context: Mock job interview for a senior product manager role.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: Tell me about a product decision you made with incomplete data. How did you approach it?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: At my last role we had to decide whether to rebuild our checkout flow before Black Friday, three weeks out. We had mixed signals from A/B tests. I triangulated: qualitative user sessions, a competitor teardown, and gut-checked with our top customers. We shipped a targeted fix rather than a full rebuild.
lines.note: Strong: shows structured thinking under pressure.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: What would you have done differently with more time?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: I would have run the full cohort analysis we skipped. We got lucky, the fix held, but I'd rather not rely on luck for revenue-critical paths.

dialogue.footer: Use this as a practice script, the interviewer lines are yours to adapt.

variants.title: Tone Variants

variants.label: Professional
variants.text: This issue is blocking our release, prioritizing a fix by end of day would be greatly appreciated.

variants.label: Direct
variants.text: This is blocking us. Please fix it today.

variants.label: Collaborative
variants.text: We're a bit stuck on this one, any chance we can tackle it together this afternoon?
variants.note: Good for teammates you know well.

variants.footer: Pick the tone that fits the relationship.

screenplay.title: Scene — The Last Train
screenplay.caption: A short night-platform scene: two strangers, one departing train.

elements.text: Fluorescent light hums over an empty platform. MAYA (30s), coat buttoned to the chin, watches the departure board flicker. A man, ELLIOT (40s), steps from the shadows of the far stairwell, out of breath.
Thirty seconds ago. You can still see the tail lights if you lean out far enough to regret it.
Elliot lets his shoulders drop. He almost laughs.

socialpost.title: Post Preview
socialpost.body: Shipped the new onboarding flow today, three months of user interviews boiled down to four screens instead of eleven. Early numbers are already trending up, and none of it would have happened without the design and support teams grinding through QA all week.
